title: Multi-User Security of Even–Mansour and Blinded Hash
summary: The source identifies ARP/ARS as a route to multi-user security analysis, while controlling cross-collisions among independent keys remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Develop a multi-user security analysis of the Even--Mansour construction and, for the function setting, an analogous analysis of blinded hash, viewing mutually independent round keys as distinct user keys. The analysis should apply the ARP/ARS machinery while carefully controlling cross-collision events arising from the use of multiple keys; handling these events is the unresolved technical obstacle.

scope.domain: Multi-user security analysis of the Even–Mansour block-cipher construction and blinded hash in the function setting.
assumptions: Round keys are mutually independent and are viewed as distinct user keys.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish the multi-user analyses using ARP/ARS while controlling cross-collision events caused by multiple independent keys.

citations.label: Post-quantum Security of Key-Alternating Feistel Ciphers

progress.summary: The source proposes ARP/ARS as the machinery for a multi-user analysis of Even–Mansour or blinded hash. It identifies cross-collision events under multiple keys as the unresolved technical obstacle.
